morphology_keys.habit: Low trailing/procumbent to decumbent herb, often under 15 cm tall; several-stemmed from the base.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate; mostly arrow-shaped with backward-pointing basal lobes, but may become more broadly lobed; soft-hairy/velvety.
morphology_keys.sepals: Outer sepals roughly 7–7.5 mm in Williamson County material, rounded/cupped and densely hairy.
morphology_keys.corolla: Broadly funnel-shaped, around 15 mm long and about 20 mm across; white with pink/rose-toned panels.
morphology_keys.fruit: Small capsule; calyx persists around fruit.

ecology.regional_note: Documented in Williamson County and broadly native from the central U.S. into Mexico.

roles: 3 photos from one multi-photo Texas/Central Texas observation when available
